rationale: X is concise and covers nearly all of the requested cross-adapter behaviors, but it gives a materially wrong acceptance expectation for invalid or non-unique `unique_by:` values on the bang form. In this revision, PostgreSQL and SQLite validate those targets for `insert_all`, while `insert_all!` bypasses unique-index resolution and accepts the option without a missing-index error. Because the scenario expressly requires the baseline for both forms, this ambiguity would misdirect implementation or review, whereas the references preserve the distinction.

shortcomings.summary: X incorrectly generalizes the PostgreSQL/SQLite `No unique index` error to invalid `unique_by:` values without excluding `insert_all!`.
shortcomings.evidence: X.md:67-70 says invalid or non-unique targets raise `ArgumentError` for PostgreSQL/SQLite with no method qualifier. `activerecord/lib/active_record/relation.rb:853-854` invokes `InsertAll` with `on_duplicate: :raise` for `insert_all!`, and `activerecord/lib/active_record/insert_all.rb:41` resolves and validates the unique index only when `@on_duplicate != :raise`; lines 193-195 only reject the option when the adapter lacks conflict-target support. The focused tests at `activerecord/test/cases/insert_all_test.rb:283-296` assert missing-index errors only for `insert_all` and `upsert_all`, while lines 115-140 show bang merely accepts `unique_by:` and still raises normal uniqueness violations. R2.md:155-163 states the resulting skip-versus-bang distinction explicitly.

strengths.summary: X is substantially more concise than both references while retaining the requested adapter matrix and broad edge-case coverage.
strengths.evidence: The executed `wc -l` comparison measured X.md at 120 lines versus R1.md at 260 and R2.md at 264; X.md:46-99 still covers adapter capabilities, default and named conflicts, composite keys, returning variants, empty and mismatched input, casting/serialization, timestamps, and skip-versus-bang atomicity.
